'''Franck Laloë''' (born May 28, 1940)<ref name=cv>{{Cite web |last=Laloë |first=Franck |title=Notice des travaux scientifiques |url=http://www.phys.ens.fr/~laloe/notice.PDF}}</ref> is a French quantum physicist, author, and open archive initiator.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-05-28 |title=Should you store treasured data on disks? |language=en-GB |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/click_online/8711747.stm |access-date=2022-12-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chicheportiche {{!}} |first=Par Olivier |title=CD et DVD ne sont pas fiables, selon l'Académie des Sciences |url=https://www.zdnet.fr/actualites/cd-et-dvd-ne-sont-pas-fiables-selon-l-academie-des-sciences-39750471.htm |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=ZDNet France |date=29 March 2010 |language=fr}}</ref> He is emeritus research director at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS).

== Education and career ==

Laloë was born in [[Rabat]], [[Morocco]] and studied physics at the [[École Polytechnique]] in Paris from 1960 to 1962. He studied at [[University of Paris VI]] (later ''Pierre and Marie Curie University'') for a two-part doctorate. His PhD from 1963 to 1968 (Doctorat de troisième cycle) involved research on spin-polarized helium-3 systems. He obtained [[Doctorat d'État]] in 1970. He worked for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and became director from 1978.<ref name=cv /> Later Laloë worked at the [[Kastler–Brossel Laboratory]] in Paris, where he was the director from 2004 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Franck Laloë |url=https://www.babelio.com/auteur/Franck-Lalo/171213 |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=Babelio |language=fr}}</ref>

Laloë is the initiator of the [[open archive]] for scientific works, [[HAL (open archive)|HAL]], created in 2001 at the [[Centre pour la communication scientifique directe]] (CCSD) of the [[Cnrs|CNRS]]. He deals with digital archiving on optical media (CD and DVD) and is president of a corresponding research group (GIS-DON).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Baruch |first=Pierre |date=2007 |title=Open access developments in France: the HAL Open Archives System |journal=Learned Publishing |language=en |volume=20 |issue=4 |pages=267–282 |doi=10.1087/095315107X239636|s2cid=206006154 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Laloë's research deals with [[optical pumping]], acoustics (including chaos), [[superfluid helium-3]], [[Quantum foundations|foundations of quantum mechanics]] and ultracold quantum gases ([[Bose einstein condensates|Bose-Einstein condensates]]), as well as optical information storage technology.<ref name=cv /><ref name=academie-sciences/> Laloë is co-author of ''[[Quantum Mechanics (book)|Quantum Mechanics]]'' ({{Langx|fr|Mécanique quantique}}), a popular series of quantum mechanics textbook with {{Ill|Bernard Diu|fr}} and [[Claude Cohen-Tannoudji]].

== Honors and awards ==

Laloë received the [[Prix de l'État]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1988,<ref name=academie-sciences>{{cite web |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_etat_physique09.pdf |title=Prix fondé par l'État physique: lauréats - Prix de l'Académie des sciences |website=academie-sciences.fr |language=fr |date=2009 |access-date=2022-12-13}}</ref> the Prix [[Aimé Cotton]] in 1970 from the [[Société Française de Physique]], and in 2000 the [[Three Physicists Prize|Prix des trois physiciens]] from the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris and the Eugène Bloch Foundation.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}}
